Recently, Bruinier and Ono classified cusp forms $f(z) := \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a_f(n)q ^n \in S_{\lambda+1/2}(\Gamma_0(N),\chi)\cap \mathbb{Z}[[q]]$ that does not satisfy a certain distribution property for modulo odd primes $p$. In this paper, using Rankin-Cohen Bracket, we extend this result to modular forms of half integral weight for primes $p \geq 5$. As applications of our main theorem we derive distribution properties, for modulo primes $p\geq5$, of traces of singular moduli and Hurwitz class number. We also study an analogue of Newman's conjecture for overpartitions.

outputs.L3:
Bruinier and Ono previously classified half-integral-weight cusp forms with integer coefficients whose Fourier coefficients fail to satisfy a prescribed distribution property modulo odd primes. Building on their work, this paper extends the classification from cusp forms to the broader setting of half-integral-weight modular forms for primes \(p \geq 5\). A central ingredient in this extension is the Rankin–Cohen bracket, which makes it possible to relate the relevant modular forms to cusp forms and thereby apply the earlier classification framework.

The paper’s main theorem has several arithmetic consequences. In particular, it establishes distribution properties modulo primes \(p \geq 5\) for traces of singular moduli, showing that these traces exhibit the expected range of residue classes under the hypotheses of the theorem. Similar arguments yield corresponding distribution results for Hurwitz class numbers, which arise naturally as coefficients of half-integral-weight modular forms.

Finally, the paper investigates an analogue of Newman’s conjecture in the context of overpartitions. By studying the modular forms associated with overpartition-generating functions, the authors examine the distribution of overpartition numbers modulo primes and connect this question with the broader theory developed in the paper.
outputs.L4:
This paper studies the distribution modulo odd primes of Fourier coefficients of half-integral-weight modular forms. Bruinier and Ono previously classified half-integral-weight cusp forms whose coefficients fail to satisfy certain expected distribution properties modulo an odd prime. We extend their approach to a broader class of half-integral-weight modular forms when the prime \(p\ge 5\). The principal tool is the theory of Rankin–Cohen brackets, which allows forms that are not necessarily cuspidal to be related to cusp forms while retaining sufficient control over their Fourier coefficients modulo \(p\). This makes it possible to apply and generalize the earlier classification results.

The resulting framework has several arithmetic applications. We obtain congruence and distribution results modulo \(p\) for generating functions associated with traces of singular moduli and with Hurwitz class numbers. In particular, the coefficients arising from these arithmetic sequences exhibit broad distribution among residue classes modulo \(p\), subject to the exceptional cases identified by the structural theory of half-integral-weight forms.

We also apply these methods to the overpartition function. Motivated by Newman’s conjecture on the distribution of ordinary partition numbers modulo an integer, we formulate and investigate an analogous question for overpartitions. The modular-form interpretation of the overpartition generating function, together with the Rankin–Cohen bracket construction and the coefficient-distribution results developed here, yields evidence and partial results toward the expectation that overpartition numbers attain prescribed residue classes modulo primes infinitely often. Thus, the paper both enlarges the scope of the Bruinier–Ono theory and demonstrates its relevance to several important arithmetic sequences.
outputs.L5: Recently, Jan Hendrik Bruinier and Ken Ono established striking connections between partition numbers, harmonic Maass forms, and algebraic number theory. Their work provides finite algebraic formulas for the partition function \(p(n)\), replacing earlier expressions that depended on infinite series. In particular, they showed that partition numbers can be recovered from traces of special values of modular functions at complex multiplication points. This result illustrates how a seemingly elementary counting problem is governed by the deep arithmetic structure of modular forms. Bruinier and Ono’s ideas have since influenced research on mock modular forms, quadratic forms, and related questions in number theory.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize a research article that uses Rankin–Cohen brackets to generalize the Bruinier–Ono classification of cusp forms failing certain coefficient-distribution properties modulo odd primes.
counterfactuals.output:
The article studies Fourier coefficients of half-integral-weight cusp forms modulo an odd prime \(\ell\). Bruinier and Ono had shown that such coefficients are normally well distributed among residue classes modulo \(\ell\); failure of this behavior can occur only for highly exceptional forms whose reductions modulo \(\ell\) are supported on finitely many square classes—essentially theta-series-type forms.

The paper extends this classification to a broader range of weights and modular-form settings. Its main tool is the Rankin–Cohen bracket, a bilinear differential operator that combines modular forms while preserving modularity. By taking brackets with suitable theta or Eisenstein series and then reducing modulo \(\ell\), the authors convert assumptions about sparse or biased coefficient distributions into modular identities. Weight and filtration arguments force these identities to vanish or impose strong congruence restrictions.

The resulting dichotomy is:

- generically, the Fourier coefficients are well distributed modulo \(\ell\);  
- if they are not, the form modulo \(\ell\) must lie in a small, explicitly constrained theta-type exceptional family, often supported on one or finitely many square classes.

Thus the article strengthens the Bruinier–Ono result by enlarging the class of forms covered and giving a systematic Rankin–Cohen-bracket method for detecting and classifying every obstruction to coefficient equidistribution. Conceptually, it shows that poor distribution modulo odd primes is not accidental: it reflects rigid theta-series structure in the modular form.

By combining the Shimura correspondence with Hecke operators, quadratic twisting, and mod-\(\ell\) reduction, we establish criteria ensuring systematic congruences among the Fourier coefficients \(a_f(n)\). counterfactuals.prompt: Can you produce a short paper summary about modular forms of half-integral weight modulo primes \(p\geq 5\), emphasizing Rankin–Cohen brackets, traces of singular moduli, Hurwitz class numbers, and an analogue of Newman’s conjecture for overpartitions?
counterfactuals.output:
### Summary

The paper develops a theory of modular forms of half-integral weight modulo primes \(p\ge 5\), extending familiar tools from the integral-weight setting. A central role is played by Rankin–Cohen brackets, whose modularity and coefficient formulas provide a way to study filtrations, theta operators, and congruences modulo \(p\). These brackets yield structural restrictions on half-integral-weight forms and help prove that certain generating functions cannot be supported on only a small set of square classes.

The theory is applied to arithmetic generating functions of weight \(3/2\). In particular, the paper studies traces of singular moduli—traces of values of modular functions at CM points—and Hurwitz class numbers. Their generating series are modular or mock-modular objects closely related to Zagier’s weight-\(3/2\) Eisenstein series. After suitable holomorphic corrections, the Rankin–Cohen and filtration machinery gives nonvanishing and divisibility results for these coefficients modulo \(p\), showing that their congruence behavior is governed by the underlying half-integral-weight modular structure.

A further application concerns the overpartition function \(\overline p(n)\), whose generating function is the eta-quotient
\[
\sum_{n\ge0}\overline p(n)q^n=\frac{\eta(2z)}{\eta(z)^2}.
\]
By converting this weakly holomorphic form into a suitable half-integral-weight modular form modulo \(p\), the paper proves an overpartition analogue of Newman’s conjecture: in the prime-modulus setting, multiples of \(p\) occur infinitely often among the values \(\overline p(n)\). More broadly, the result illustrates how mod-\(p\) half-integral-weight theory can turn modular identities into concrete distribution and divisibility statements for class numbers, CM traces, and partition-type functions.
